steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Natural fibres: cotton (breathable, absorbent, soft), wool (warm, elastic, fire-resistant), silk (strong, lustrous, drapes well), linen (cool, crisp, creases easily).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Synthetic fibres: polyester (durable, quick-dry, wrinkle-resistant), nylon (strong, abrasion-resistant), elastane/Lycra (extreme stretch and recovery).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Woven fabrics: warp and weft interlaced at 90 degrees - stable, strong, limited stretch. Plain weave, twill weave (denim), satin weave.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Knitted fabrics: interlocking loops - stretchy, comfortable, can ladder. Weft knit (t-shirts) vs warp knit (more stable, swimwear).

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Explain why polycotton is used for school shirts instead of 100% cotton or 100% polyester. | Compare woven and knitted fabric constructions, explaining why each suits different garments. | Discuss the environmental impact of synthetic fibres compared to natural fibres.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: 100% cotton: comfortable but creases badly, shrinks. 100% polyester: durable and wrinkle-free but feels clammy, does not breathe. Polycotton (typically 65/35): retains cotton's breathability, gains po | Woven: warp + weft at 90 degrees, stable, holds shape - suits structured garments (shirts, trousers). Knitted: interlocking loops, stretchy, comfortable - suits body-hugging garments (t-shirts, socks, | Synthetic: petrochemicals (non-renewable), microplastic shedding, non-biodegradable, but durable and recyclable. Natural: renewable, biodegradable, but cotton needs vast water and pesticides. Neither

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know the difference between fibre (raw strand), yarn (spun fibres) and fabric (woven/knitted) Specify the fibre type - 'polyester' not just 'synthetic' Blend rationale: explain which property each fibre contributes to the blend
